::::{#thm-local-constant}
#### A local constant fit is a kernel-weighted average

In @def-local-regression,
suppose the local polynomial has degree 0 (a constant $a$),
and let $w_i \ge 0$ be the kernel weight of observation $i$ at the target point $x_0$,
with $\sum_{i=1}^n w_i > 0$.
Then the weighted least-squares fit at $x_0$ is the weighted average

$$
\est{f}(x_0) = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n w_i y_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n w_i}
$$

[@hastie2009esl2e, §6.1].
::::
